title: Affine-local canonical truncation comparison for higher direct image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], $q\in\mathbf Z$, and let $U\subseteq Y$ be an affine open. For some $n\in\mathbf Z$, the restriction to $U$ of the canonical map $H^q(Rf_*E)\to H^q(Rf_*\tau_{\geq -n}E)$ is an isomorphism. Here $Rf_*$ is [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and the truncation and its projection are [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. No quasi-coherence assertion about either side is included.

proof.text: Put V = f⁻¹(U) and g = f ∣_ U. Mathlib supplies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of g by restriction, and compactness of U because U is affine. Choose the standard derived categories of the two open subschemes; the original derived categories of X and Y remain unchanged.

Let RX and RY be the exact restriction functors, each followed by Scheme.Modules.overEquiv. Quasi-coherence is preserved by overFunctor and by the site equivalence (transport the quasi-coherent presentation using isQuasicoherent_pushforward_of_isLeftAdjoint). The natural homology comparison RX.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso then shows that RX.mapDerivedCategory.obj E lies in D_QCoh(V). Use schemeDerivedDirectImage_openRestriction for the natural isomorphism Rf_* ⋙ D(RY) ≅ D(RX) ⋙ Rg_*; its K-injective computation is already contained in that theorem.

Apply the second clause of exists_schemeDerivedDirectImage_uniform_truncation_bound to g, the restricted quasi-coherent derived object, and q. Take n to be the supplied threshold, using n ≤ n. Thus H^q(Rg_*) maps the canonical projection of the restricted object to an isomorphism.

Set π to be the global truncation projection. Let c be the inverse component of RX.mapDerivedCategoryTruncGEIso (-n). The defining equation π_descTruncGE gives π_restricted ≫ c = D(RX).map π. Both H^q(Rg_*).map π_restricted and H^q(Rg_*).map c are isomorphisms, so their composite is. Apply NatIso.isIso_map_iff first to the open-restriction isomorphism whiskered by homology, then to RY.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso q. This proves that RY maps H^q(Rf_*).map π to an isomorphism. The equivalence component of RY reflects isomorphisms, yielding exactly the requested overFunctor map.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_isIso_schemeHigherDirectImage_truncGE_over_affine
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hE : schemeDerivedQCohProperty X E)
    (q : ℤ) (U : Y.affineOpens) :
    ∃ n : ℤ, IsIso
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) U.1).map
        ((schemeHigherDirectImage f q).map
          ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-n)).app E)))
